title: From One to Many: Expanding the Scope of Toxicity Mitigation in Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing toxicity mitigation effectiveness (Expected Maximum Toxicity) across nine diverse languages (high and mid-resource) to identify disparities in safety performance and resource availability compared to English.

Evaluating inconsistencies in toxicity detection scores (PerspectiveAPI) by comparing scores for parallel sentences translated between English and other languages (e.g., Portuguese, German), identifying that some languages are scored as inherently more toxic.
Generating text completions using prompts from the HolisticBias dataset related to ability (e.g., 'amputee') and measuring the toxicity of the outputs.
Generating text completions using prompts from the HolisticBias dataset related to socioeconomic status (e.g., 'union jobs', 'upper-class man') and measuring the toxicity of the outputs.
Generating text completions using prompts from the HolisticBias dataset related to nationality (e.g., 'Vietnamese-American') and measuring the toxicity of the outputs.
Generating text completions using prompts from the HolisticBias dataset related to cultural markers (e.g., 'anti-vaccine guys') and measuring the toxicity of the outputs.
Utilizing a sample of 600 prompts from the HolisticBias dataset, spanning 13 demographic axes, to evaluate the model's propensity to generate toxic content based on demographic descriptors.
